analysis-results.adoption.title: Adoption paths
analysis-results.adoption.definitions: The relational step moves the whole database, a cache step fronts reads and moves no data, and every other step moves one group of queries to one engine; each wave of the roadmap holds one or more steps. A step runs in stages, each with its own gate. A stage moves units: a unit is the smallest set of queries and tables that moves on its own, and each step's pilot is its first unit to move.
analysis-results.adoption.intro-relation: Each path is this plan stopped after one of its steps: it takes steps 1 to that step, and the queries of every later step stay on {{engine}}. The staged full target is the default; an earlier stop is a smaller end state.

graph-explorer.help.title: About the explorer
graph-explorer.help.graph: Source tables are small rectangles with the table icon; destination engines are rounded squares showing the engine's AWS service icon, with its name. Each query is a link from every table it touches to its engine; the queries between one table and one engine are bundled into one straight link until you fan it out into curved per-query links. Link width is traffic (calls per second, on a log scale), and busy links pull their table close to its engine.
graph-explorer.help.click: Click a table or engine to expand it, a bundle to fan it out into its queries, a query link to see its details. Drag a node and its neighbours follow; when you let go it stays there, pinned (a dotted outline), and the rest keeps its place. Double-click a pinned node, or use Unpin in Details, to release it; Reset layout releases them all. The query list on the left follows the graph both ways.
graph-explorer.help.views: Traffic sizes links by calls per second; Moves together marks the queries that move as one unit; Who writes draws each table's writer solid and replica reads dashed; Cost sizes engines by monthly cost.
graph-explorer.help.filters: Filter by engine, by minimum traffic, or by wave: what moves in the wave is drawn in full, the reads its cache fronts a little lighter, the queries that only cut over in it dimmer.
graph-explorer.help.walkthroughs: Walkthroughs follow the assessment's own reasoning: the migration wave by wave and the table groups in each wave, the busiest queries and why each landed where it did, and why each engine. Each step sets the graph; explore from there, then go to the next step.
graph-explorer.help.limits: Waves, units, each table's source of truth, the cache layer and costs are read from the job's files with the same code the context graph holds them from. The view draws at most 150 nodes and links. The deliverables and the results page remain the reference.

graph-explorer.filters.other-waves-note: Greyed out for context, or hidden.
graph-explorer.help.waves: Picking a wave (as a start point, a walkthrough step or the wave filter) draws what moves in that wave in full, the reads its cache layer fronts a little lighter, and the queries that only cut over in it dimmer. Everything else already in the graph stays visible, greyed out, with its own move wave on hover (and under a greyed engine's name). Thin grey dashed links are cross-wave links: a table in the wave linked to something that moves in another wave, which shows what the wave still connects to. Turn off "Show other waves" in Filters to hide the rest instead.
graph-explorer.legend.pinned: Dotted outline: pinned where you dropped it (double-click to release)

graph-explorer.help.questions: The Questions tab lists the graph query catalog: fixed, read-only questions about this job, such as the busiest queries or what a table's change would touch. Pick a question, choose its parameters from the values the graph holds (or type one when the list is cut short; the server checks it), and run it. The rows show as a table, with how many there are and whether more matched; an empty result says which pipeline stages left nothing to read. Show on graph draws the result as a new start, from its tables first: its own tables and engines are outlined in blue and the links carrying its queries are blue. There is no free-form query.
